newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says Jan M3 boosted by statistical factors.
newsitem.headline: Buba says Jan M3 boosted by statistical factors.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday January M3 money supply growth was boosted by a strong statistical "overhang" at the end of 1996, by weak money capital formation and by strong bank lending to the public sector.
The central bank also noted that annualised money supply data released at the beginning of any year tended to be subject to sharp swings because of the brief period that was being annualised.
The Bundesbank said that M3 grew at an annualised rate of 11.7 percent in January from the fourth quarter of 1996, above expectations for a growth rate of between 4.5 percent and 8.2 percent.

The Bundesbank also published annualised January M3 growth compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, saying this would reduce problems in interpreting the January data because it had the same basis as used for M3 data last year.
Based on the final quarter of 1995, January M3 grew at an annualised rate of 8.6 percent compared with 7.9 percent growth in December.
The Bundesbank noted that money supply expansion in January was dampened by weakening loan demand in the private sector and heavy money outflows abroad.
But there was strong growth in sight deposits, short-term deposits and standard savings deposits with three-month notice of withdrawal, the Bundesbank said. Cash in circulation fell.
Money capital formation at banks virtually came to a standstill in January on a seasonally-adjusted basis, the Bundesbank said.

"The historically low level of capital market rates and fairly marked volatility in the bond market appear to have acted as a strong brake on the willingness of investors to make longer-term investments," the Bundesbank said.
Over the last six months, money capital formation at banks grew at an annualised rate of 4 1/2 percent.
Bank lending to companies and private individuals grew at a seasonally-adjusted annualised rate of 7 1/2 percent over the last six months, the Bundesbank said.

It added that bank lending to the private sector had weakened significantly in January after having been strong in December ahead of the reduction of tax breaks for new rented accommodation in east Germany.

The Bundesbank also said expanded M3, which includes domestic investment by non-banks in money market funds, grew at a seasonally-adjusted annualised rate of 4 1/2 percent in the six months through December -- two percentage points less than M3 growth in the same period. There are no extended M3 data available for January yet.
